brief: GS strategists debate where equity earnings leadership comes from next, since AI infrastructure capex drove over 35% Q3 S&P 500 earnings growth and a successor driver (lower oil/rates or continued AI advancement) is needed to avoid a broad earnings downturn. Tech indices (NDX, SOX) are oversold at over 10 year low valuations, and AI supply chain charts imply coming cuts, but near-term earnings (DELL, MU, AVGO, HPE) are expected to revise higher, leaving charts and companies in tension. Wilson frames the worry as AI financing needs and a peaking investment cycle rather than one clear macro threat, since growth tracks GS forecasts. Privorotsky reads extreme positioning (shorts at their largest since April 2025, net leverage at a 1-year low) plus extreme vol (VIX near 40, Fear and Greed near 10) as a tactical setup for a bear market rally, conditional on credit: if Nvidia rallies without neocloud spread relief, it is short covering, not recovery. Mericle says 100bp of FCI tightening this year makes a December hike near certain and a March hike likely, unless an AI spending pullback or sentiment shock displaces it. FX sees dollar strength rotating from developed to emerging markets.
